uncited: Splat Batching Strategy is a GPU optimization technique for 3D Gaussian Splatting that reduces draw call overhead by packing multiple Gaussian splats into a single instanced rendering command.
It addresses the performance bottleneck of issuing individual draw calls for each Gaussian, which is inefficient when rendering scenes with tens or hundreds of thousands of splats.

Unlike non-tiled approaches that may process all splats in one massive batch or tile-based methods that split work spatially, batching focuses on temporal efficiency by grouping splats into fixed-size chunks for instanced drawing.
The method relies on GPU instancing to render multiple geometric primitives (splat quads) with a single draw call.
Each instance corresponds to one 3D Gaussian, transformed into screen space.
- **Input:** A list of $N$ 3D Gaussians, each defined by position, covariance (or scale/rotation), opacity, and spherical harmonics coefficients.
If set to -1, all Gaussians are rendered in a single batch.
If positive, the Gaussians are split into batches of this size.
**Vertex Buffer:** An array of size $4 \times \text{SplatInstanceSize}$.
Each instance contributes 4 vertices representing the corners of a screen-space quad.
**Index Buffer:** An array of size $6 \times \text{SplatInstanceSize}$.
Each instance contributes 2 triangles (6 indices).
**Instance Buffer:** A buffer containing per-instance attributes (position, scale, rotation, opacity, SH coefficients).
**Calculate Batches:** Determine the number of batches $B = \lceil N / \text{SplatInstanceSize} \rceil$.
- Set four vertex positions at screen-space corners: $(-1,-1), (1,-1), (-1,1), (1,1)$.
This allows the fragment shader to identify the instance ID.
**Populate Instance Data:** Fill the instance buffer with the attributes for the current batch of Gaussians.
- Bind the vertex, index, and instance buffers for the current batch.
- Issue an instanced draw call (e.g., `glDrawElementsInstanced`) with `SplatInstanceSize` instances.
- The vertex shader transforms the screen-space quad into world/view space using the instance attributes.
- The fragment shader computes the 2D Gaussian contribution and blends it into the frame buffer.
- **Memory Usage:** Large batch sizes increase the size of the vertex and index buffers.
This variant focuses on the specific geometry generation for instanced rendering.
It defines the vertex and index layout for the splat quads.
Each instance represents a single Gaussian, and the mesh consists of two triangles forming a quad.
The vertices are defined in screen space with corners at $(-1,-1), (1,-1), (-1,1), (1,1)$, and the Z coordinate is set to the instance index to allow the fragment shader to identify the instance.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N)$ where $N$ is the number of Gaussians.
The number of draw calls is reduced to $O(N / \text{SplatInstanceSize})$.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(\text{SplatInstanceSize})$ for the vertex and index buffers per batch.
The instance buffer size is also proportional to the batch size.
- **Limitations:** Requires careful management of batch sizes to balance memory and performance; may not be suitable for dynamic scenes with frequent updates if buffer updates are expensive.
Splat Batching Strategy is derived from the broader field of 3D Gaussian Splatting, which was introduced by Kerbl et al. in 2023.
These implementations aim to optimize the rendering pipeline for real-time applications on GPUs.
